title: RBACv2 evidence simulations & auditor QnA kit
body:
Purpose
This working playbook provides a set of reproducible evidence simulation scenarios, SIEM query recipes, control-to-evidence mapping, and an auditor Q&A primer focused on RBAC v2, audit log schema, and evidence automation for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 reviews. It is intended as a hands-on kit the SRE/Security engineer can run during pre-audit dry-runs and as a short Q&A script for auditor interviews.

Scope
- RBAC v2: role definitions, permission inheritance, policy changes, admin escalations, service-account behavior.
- Audit log schema: required fields (actor, action, resource, outcome, request_id, timestamp, metadata), retention, immutability markers.
- Evidence automation: scripts for packaging exports, checksum & provenance metadata, S3/SIEM exports.
- SIEM export: typical ingest formats (JSON lines), sample search queries for Splunk/Elastic.

Quick TL;DR findings (dry-run summary)
- Most of the RBAC model is implemented but we lack standardized labels for transient escalation events (temporary-grant requests) in the log schema — creates an evidence gap for control AC-5 (ISO) / CC6.0 (SOC 2).
- SIEM export pipeline timestamps are normalized to UTC but the event_time vs. ingestion_time fields get swapped in edge cases (k8s node restarts) — affects reconstruction accuracy for a subset of events.
- Evidence packaging automation exists but does not embed a persistent provenance manifest linking each exported file to the source request_id and export job id.

Control-to-evidence map (examples)
- ISO A.9.2.2 / SOC2 CC: Access provisioning - Evidence: user provisioning audit logs (path: s3://redwood-sec-evidence/rbacv2/provisioning/YYYY-MM-DD.csv), linked export job id (export_job:exp-20241122-09).
- ISO A.9.4.1 / SOC2 CC: Access review - Evidence: monthly access-review CSV + reconciliation script outputs, Confluence review minutes (confluence:SEC-RBACV2-REVIEWS/2024-11).
- ISO A.12.4.1 / SOC2 CC: Logging events - Evidence: SIEM export snapshot (siem:archive/2024-11-22/rbacv2.jsonl), audit schema spec (confluence:SEC-AUDIT-SCHEMA-v2).

Evidence artifacts we will generate in simulations
- 1) Simulated role-change event stream (10k events) with request_id, actor_id, prior_roles, new_roles, reason, token_id, outcome. Stored: s3://redwood-sec-evidence/simulations/role-change-20241122.jsonl
- 2) Admin escalation scenario (timeboxed grant + automated revoke) with correlated entries in: auth-service logs, orchestration trace, SIEM export.
- 3) Orphaned service-account creation + automated detection/alert (will surface in SIEM as ALERT:SVC-ORPHAN-2024-11).

SIEM search recipes (copy/paste)
- Splunk (search head) — find role changes by user alice@example.com in last 7d:
index=rbac_events sourcetype=rbac:events actor.email="alice@example.com" action=role_change | stats count by new_roles, prior_roles, request_id, _time

- Elastic (KQL) — admin escalation sequences where grant is not followed by revoke within 24h:
sequence where event.action: "grant_role" -> event.action: "revoke_role" within 24h and event.outcome: "success" is false | display event.request_id, actor.id, timeframe

- Generic JSONL filter (local) — command-line filter to extract events missing 'request_id':
jq 'select(.request_id == null)' rbacv2-export-20241122.jsonl > missing-requestid.jsonl

SIEM export schema snippet (required fields; example line)
- Required top-level fields: timestamp, request_id, actor_id, actor_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome, ip_address, service_name, ingestion_time, export_job_id, signature_checksum.
- Example event (single-line JSON):
{
  "timestamp": "2024-11-22T09:12:03Z",
  "request_id": "req-4f7a2c",
  "actor_id": "user:alice@example.com",
  "actor_type": "user",
  "action": "grant_role",
  "resource_type": "role",
  "resource_id": "role:dev-admin",
  "outcome": "success",
  "ip_address": "34.68.21.9",
  "service_name": "auth-service",
  "ingestion_time": "2024-11-22T09:12:05Z",
  "export_job_id": "exp-20241122-09",
  "signature_checksum": "sha256:3a7b..."
}

Simulation runbook (minimal reproducible steps)
- Preconditions: test tenant with 50 users + 12 roles, SIEM dev index active, s3 simulation bucket writable.
- Step 0 (prepare): checkout github:repo/infrastructure/log-exporter branch sim/rbac-playbook, run `./scripts/generate-sim-events --type role-change --count 10000 --out s3://...`
- Step 1 (ingest): trigger the export job `scripts/trigger-export --job-id exp-20241122-09 --target siem` and monitor Kafka topic rbac.events.dev.
- Step 2 (validate): run Splunk/Elastic queries above; verify export_job_id is present on every event and that there are no events with ingestion_time < timestamp.
- Step 3 (package evidence): run `scripts/package-evidence --job-id exp-20241122-09 --manifest` to create evidence bundle with checksums and manifest (manifest must include: job_id, created_by, sha256 list, sample_events_count, time_range).
- Step 4 (upload & sign): upload to s3://redwood-sec-evidence/artifacts/exp-20241122-09.zip and sign the manifest with KMS key alias "alias/sec-evidence".

Auditor Q&A primer (short scripts)
- Q: How do you prove that role changes are attributable to a user and not a system process?
  A: Every role-change event includes actor_type + actor_id + source_ip + token_id and is signed at export. For high-risk changes we have an orchestration trace id cross-referenced to the provisioning workflow in GH Actions logs (linked in manifest). Demonstration: show an example event from the export, then the corresponding GH Action run recorded at github:repo/actions/runs/8962.

- Q: Can you show a failed grant attempt and how it surfaces in SIEM?
  A: Yes — run the Splunk query for outcome=failure and filter by action=grant_role. We have a sample failed attempt in the simulation (req-4f7a2c-fail) that demonstrates detection and an automated alert (ticket SEC-ALERT-311).

- Q: How do you prevent tampering with exported evidence?
  A: Evidence bundles are SHA256-signed and the manifest contains the export_job_id, S3 path, and KMS-signed signature. We maintain the export job history in an append-only ledger (logs:secure-db.export_jobs table) and back up raw SIEM snapshots to a WORM-compliant bucket for the retention window.

- Q: What about temporary/just-in-time grants?
  A: RBAC v2 emits a transient_grant=true flag for temporary grants and records timeboxed expiry and original approver id. Our simulation includes one transient grant sequence where the revoke is automated after 4 hours — this is useful for auditors to review lifecycle completeness.

Evidence checklist for a SOC2/ISO audit dry-run
- [ ] Exported SIEM snapshot: JSONL + checksum + manifest.
- [ ] Export job record with human approver + run logs.
- [ ] Mapping doc of control IDs -> artifact names (Confluence link).
- [ ] Sample incident ticket and alert rule (ticket:SEC-ALERT-311).
- [ ] Proof of retention configuration (S3 bucket policy + WORM backup note).
- [ ] Signed manifest (KMS key alias).

Open issues / action items (for next sprint)
- [AIS-1] Add persistent request_id for service-to-service retries — currently a small percent of retry storms generate duplicate request_ids (owner: Liam).
- [AIS-2] Add export manifest field linking to Confluence runbook and reviewer id (owner: Priya).
- [AIS-3] Harden ingestion_time normalization code path for node-restart edge-case (owner: Evan).

Appendix: sample outputs to show auditors quickly
- Where to find simulation bundle: s3://redwood-sec-evidence/simulations/role-change-20241122.jsonl
- Evidence bundle (zip): s3://redwood-sec-evidence/artifacts/exp-20241122-09.zip
- Proof-of-signature (KMS): kms:alias/sec-evidence:signature-20241122
- Quick demo script to run locally: `./scripts/dryrun-audit-kit --job exp-20241122-09 --verify`

Notes to reviewers
- This is a living working doc intended for pre-audit dry-runs. Add any failed queries, missing fields, or auditor follow-ups directly in the Confluence ticket (confluence:SEC-RBACV2-ISSUES-2024) and tag the evidence bundle id.

Unresolved auditor questions to flag early
- During a real audit, an external auditor may ask for cross-system correlation across GitHub, KMS, and SIEM exports. We need a simple mapping table that ties export_job_id -> GH run id -> KMS signature id. Currently this mapping exists in the export_job table but is not surfaced in the manifest (see AIS-2).

End of doc
